trial_court: District Judge, Jorhat in Title Suit (M) 79/2011
case_name: Sri Ranjan Baruah vs Smti Shravani Khound Baruah
facts_of_case: Appellant married respondent on 02.05.2004. Out of wedlock, a girl child was born to the couple. The couple fell out and respondent started misbehaving with appellant's old parents. Appellant filed application under Section 13(1) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 praying for decree of dissolution of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty is a state of mind.
legal_principles.held: The feeling of deep anguish, disappointment, frustration in one spouse caused by the conduct of other for a long time may lead to mental cruelty.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: Mere coldness or lack of affection cannot amount to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: Frequent rudeness of language, petulance of manner, indifference and neglect may reach such a degree that it makes the married life for the other spouse absolutely intolerable.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty is a sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment.
legal_principles.held: A sustained course of abusive and humiliating treatment calculated to torture, discommode or render miserable life of the spouse.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

outcome.final_order: The final court order dissolved the marriage.

use_for_drafting: assisting with joint family property disputes
